newsitem.title: UK: Britain says it is killing 55,000 cows a week.
newsitem.headline: Britain says it is killing 55,000 cows a week.

text.p: The British government said on Sunday it was slaughtering cows at a rate of 55,000 every week to try to eradicate mad cow disease.

It said 730,000 cattle had already been killed under a plan to slaughter all cattle over 30 months old -- those considered most at risk of developing Boving Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease).
The European Union wants a further 147,000 cattle destroyed in a "selective cull" before it will lift a world-wide ban on British beef exports.

But the British government baulked at this, citing an Oxford University report that suggested BSE would die out in Britain on its own by 2001 and a cull would do little to hasten the disease's demise.

The cattle now being slaughtered are incinerated, but there is a backlog because of a shortage of facilities. The government said it had speeded up the process by rendering some of the parts of the carcasses before they are put into cold storage to await incineration.
